QF.id: Analysis of Equity and Debt Instruments_6

question.text: Anita holds Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) with a face value of Rs.5,00,000. She receives annual interest of Rs.12,500. At maturity after 8 years, the redemption value is Rs.8,50,000. What is the total tax liability on the SGB for Anita (an individual in the 30% slab)?

answer.text: Tax on interest (Rs.12,500 × 8 × 30%) + LTCG on redemption at 12.5%
No tax — both interest and redemption gains are exempt for individuals
Tax only on interest income at slab rate (Rs.12,500 × 8 × 30% = Rs.30,000 over 8 years). Redemption gain is exempt
Tax on interest at 10% TDS rate + LTCG at 12.5% on redemption

explanation.text: The Logic: SGB interest of 2.5% p.a. on the nominal value is taxable as "Income from Other Sources" at the investor's slab rate. For Anita at 30%, the annual tax is Rs.12,500 × 30% = Rs.3,750, totaling Rs.30,000 over 8 years. Redemption of SGBs by an individual is not treated as a transfer and the capital gain on redemption is fully exempt for individuals, so the Rs.3,50,000 gain on maturity (Rs.8,50,000 - Rs.5,00,000) attracts zero tax. The Trap: Option A wrongly applies LTCG on redemption. Option D incorrectly assumes TDS on SGB interest — SGBs are Government Securities and the workbook is explicit that no TDS is deducted on SGB interest; the individual investor pays the slab-rate tax directly. Note: The exemption is specific to redemption by an individual. If SGBs are sold on the exchange before maturity, the gain is taxable as capital gains under the normal rules for listed securities.
